correctness.rationale: At the first zero proposal, the negative feedback derivative is the validation projection onto the training direction divided by the training norm. Conditional on the training vector, the standardized projection has a fixed standard normal law, independent of the chi-square radius; the common sigma/sqrt(b) cancels. Projection yields the stated law and atoms. The second update uses fresh samples; at fixed p>0 the acceptance condition is a one-sided normal test at p sqrt(U_d)/2. Weighting by the true squared displacement multiplies the chi-square density by U_d, exactly d times the chi-square_(d+2) density. At p=0 the tie cannot affect risk; A_d(0)=1/2 is the continuous tail extension, not the actual tie acceptance probability. For d=1, rescale the Cauchy integral by y=eta r; the limiting coefficient is [integral_0^M A_1(y) dy+M A_1(M)]/pi, and integrating the t_3-ratio tail using (p arctan(p/2))' gives the printed positive formula. For d=2, r^2 rho_2(r)=1/(2r)+O(r^-3) above r=1; the Lipschitz tail A_2(eta r)=1/2+O(eta r) up to r=M/eta changes the clipped logarithmic contribution only by O_M(eta^2), as does the saturated tail. Above d=2 the clipped risk is dominated after eta^-2 rescaling by (R_d)_+^2, of mean 1/[2(d-2)]. Replacing the acceptance factor by one checks all proposal constants. These arguments verify RESULT.md lines 55–109 at fixed M,b,sigma,d. The self-review's 70 finite checks are reported in VERIFICATION.md; check.py was inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: A noisy validation null step is designed to protect the primal iterate, so its exact residual risk at a noninterpolating optimum is a natural diagnostic. Even when larger batches reduce this risk by 1/b, they do not stabilize the normalized feedback law. The critical dimensions and exact factors quantify how the safeguard and cap modify the risk, separating a heavy-tail boundary layer from a finite-moment regime. This is a specific mechanism, not a claim about eventual convergence or a new optimizer.
